acceptance: pytest tests/test_repo_hygiene_observe.py passes: 14+ temp-repo cases covering clean, dirty-tracked, dirty-untracked, ahead-of-remote, no-upstream, merged-into-default, detached HEAD, zero-commit, no-remote, and cap-tripped repos. Critically, the detached-HEAD, zero-commit, and no-remote cases each carry a populated tree section when the tree is dirty and branches=None — dirty work is reported in exactly the repos where branch analysis cannot run. Only a non-repo cwd returns None overall, and no case raises.

pytest tests/test_repo_hygiene_classify.py passes: classify() is verified pure (monkeypatched subprocess.run and Path.write_text raise if touched); a branch that is both merged and ahead emits exactly one finding and it is the merged one; the default branch, the current branch, and a branch checked out in a second worktree each produce zero cleanup findings even when otherwise qualifying; binding suppression holds; the collapse threshold is exercised at N-1, N, and N+1.

pytest tests/test_repo_hygiene_provider.py passes: every emitted item declares a clears_when in registered_predicates(); suppress_resolved() retires each kind once its predicate flips; no item has a non-None exact_command; no item asserts reversible=True without a named re-runnable remedy; ActionItem.__post_init__ accepts every item; aggregate() dedupes repeats; and per D010 every item has a non-None plain_consequence and no title leads with a git mechanism term (ahead, upstream, ref, HEAD, porcelain).

pytest tests/test_repo_hygiene_plan_status.py passes: a fixture tree containing an all-passing active plan, an all-passing draft plan, an all-passing blocked plan, an all-passing completed plan, a partially-passing active plan, and a schema-invalid plan yields exactly one command-resolvable item (the active one, whose exact_command both passes validate_command_tokens AND is accepted by close_plan in dry-run), two explanation-only status items (draft, blocked), zero for completed and partial, and one plan_unparseable advisory.

pytest tests/test_repo_hygiene_cli.py passes and behavioral evidence is captured: `dontpanic next --json` in a fixture repo with all four git conditions plus one status-drifted plan emits the expected items with correct bands and project scoping; a clean repo emits zero hygiene items; `dashboard build --project <name>` renders them scoped; a missing project path produces an uncertainty card rather than a traceback or a bespoke item shape.

pytest tests/test_repo_hygiene_safety.py passes: the runner-level allowlist assertion holds across every F001 fixture (and fails if a transitive helper issues an unlisted subcommand); the .git tree hash is identical before and after observation on all fixtures including the stale-index repo; and a token-shaped branch name is scrubbed from the rendered payload.

(1) A fixture declaring audience 'none' with neither summary nor surfaces is accepted. (2) A fixture declaring audience 'none' that also carries a summary is rejected. (3) An end-user fixture missing its summary is rejected. (4) An end-user fixture whose summary is under 10 characters is rejected. (5) An end-user fixture with an empty surfaces array is rejected. (6) The JSON Schema and the Pydantic model return the same verdict on all five fixtures.

(1) No plan directory's validation outcome changes: the same plan set validated against the pre-change and post-change schema yields an identical per-plan exit code. (2) git status shows no existing plan file modified by this feature. (3) The subtree-pulled schema in DontPanic is byte-identical to the one committed in agent-conventions.

(1) A pause emitted through the real supervisor path produces a NotifyEvent carrying a populated brief with no caller passing metadata arguments to render. (2) The attached dataclass is frozen and equality-comparable. (3) Status is declared when the recorded digest matches the current description. (4) Status is possibly-stale when the digests differ. (5) Status is undeclared when F001's impact block is absent. (6) pytest tests/test_decision_brief_delivery.py covers all five and passes.

(1) RenderedEvent exposes the three new fields with None defaults and every existing template row still constructs. (2) Round-tripping a brief through render and into ActionItem preserves the decision-consequence element exactly, for each of three distinct briefs, so the mapping is proven rather than a single fixture matching. (4) The reversible flag on an event-derived ActionItem tracks the brief across both True and False, rather than the hardcoded False it carries today. (5) pytest tests/test_event_copy_brief_fields.py covers all four and passes.

(1) A commit introducing a regression-suite failure fails the build, demonstrated on a scratch branch. (2) A commit introducing a capability-suite failure does not fail the build, demonstrated the same way. (3) Both jobs publish their reports as retrievable artifacts. (4) The gating job performs no model call. (5) CONTRIBUTING states which suite gates and how to add to each. (6) The two demonstration runs are captured under the plan's evidence directory.

(1) Driving the real _emit_gate_paused_discord with pending_gates=['pre_merge'], stage='general' renders gate `pre_merge` and stage `general` as distinct values, and no rendered slot contains the string 'gate `general`'. (2) The same holds for pending_gates=['breaker:iteration_cap'], stage='upfront': no rendered slot contains 'upfront' as a gate. (3) The two call sites that pass a non-gate stage (supervisor.py:1316 'general' and supervisor.py:2021 'upfront') are both covered by a test, and the test names them so a future re-homing of the call is caught. (4) _gather_fields no longer falls back to subtype for the gate slot, and a gate-shaped event with no pending_gates metadata renders with the gate omitted rather than substituted. (5) A multi-gate pause with pending_gates of length 2 renders a documented, runnable-or-absent command — specifically it must not print a single approve command containing a comma. (6) The stage='pre_merge' site still renders exactly as it does today, proving the change did not regress the two already-correct call sites. (7) The full existing event_copy and messaging suites pass with no new failures against a same-scope baseline.

(1) A test asserts the rendered exact_command for a gate pause on pre_merge is exactly 'dontpanic approve <plan_id> pre_merge'. (2) An invariant test iterates every renderable kind and fails if any rendered slot names a gate absent from the source event. (3) The invariant is proven non-vacuous: a deliberate mutation reintroducing the subtype-to-gate alias makes it fail, and that failure is captured as evidence. (4) The parametrized kind set is derived from the disposition table rather than hardcoded, and is asserted non-empty. (5) pytest passes for the new module and the full suite shows no new failures against a same-scope baseline.

(1) README states that the approve command names the gate that is actually pending. (2) CHANGELOG.md has an Unreleased or dated entry for this fix. (3) No second 'what is DontPanic' section is invented. (4) A reader can tell this is different from `dontpanic approve <plan> general`, the non-gate token the command used to print.
